This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #38362: OOM crash on startup when session/event data grows very large (1.4 GB DB, V8 zone allocation failure) — same symptom of the entire app being hard-bricked on startup by oversized session data, with the same manual SQLite workaround
- #32005: event table bloat from `message.updated.1` events causing OOM when loading old sessions — similar root cause of unbounded data growth leading to startup OOM

Your issue has a distinct angle (schema validation failure path + per-session graceful degradation as the fix), so it may warrant staying open independently, but it would be worth coordinating with those issues and their assignee.

This issue might be a duplicate of or a regression from existing issues. Please check:

- #29671 (closed): describes nearly identical symptoms — 6 GB+ RSS on TUI startup within seconds, Ubuntu Linux, empty directory, `--pure` flag makes no difference. That issue was closed as fixed, so if you are seeing this on v1.18.31 it may be a regression worth noting in that context.
- #20695 (closed): Memory Megathread — contains heap snapshot instructions (`OPENCODE_AUTO_HEAP_SNAPSHOT=1 opencode` or ctrl+p → heap snapshot) that would help pin the exact retainer, which you noted yourself in the issue.

If this is indeed a regression rather than a duplicate, please mention that in your report so maintainers can diff against the prior fix.

Both asks are now in `v2`:

- Following the `resource_metadata` URL from the 401 `WWW-Authenticate` challenge (path and query included) landed in #48937.
- The explicit override landed in #49126 as `oauth.auth_server_metadata_url` on remote MCP servers. Point it at the authorization server's OAuth 2.0 or OpenID Connect metadata document and it is used for both login and token refresh instead of protected resource discovery.
Closing as duplicate of #48741, which is the main tracking thread for this exact error (Zen muse-spark encrypted_content replay). See also fix PR #48918.

The `.husky/pre-push` Windows-gated workaround that was part of this PR has been extracted into a separate bug fix:

- **Bug report:** #49224 — tsgo crashes with OOM on Windows when turbo typecheck runs in parallel on heavily loaded machines
- **Fix PR:** #49228 — `fix(turbo): limit concurrency on Windows to prevent tsgo OOM`

#49228 adds `script/turbo.ts` that dynamically limits turbo's concurrency based on available commit memory. Once #49228 is merged, the workaround in `.husky/pre-push` in this PR is no longer needed (the `typecheck` script will handle it automatically). I'll rebase this PR to remove the `.husky/pre-push` change once #49228 lands.

Follow-up with a clue that might help narrow this down: the steady-state memory splits cleanly into a "live" part and a "reclaimable garbage" part.

Setting a Bun/JSC heap ceiling env var before launch, which forces more aggressive GC:

```sh
BUN_JSC_forceRAMSize=536870912 opencode .   # 512MB cap
```

...does **not** stop the initial spike (still climbs to ~7.1GB over the first ~8s, same growth curve as unconstrained), but once GC kicks in afterward, steady-state settles at **~3.6GB instead of ~6.5GB** — about a 45% reduction. I pushed the cap as low as 256MB and steady-state stayed at ~3.6GB every time — it doesn't go any lower no matter how much GC pressure is applied. Confirmed the TUI still renders and functions correctly under this setting (prompt bar, skills panel, etc. all render normally), so it's a usable stopgap, not just a crash-avoidance trick.

That suggests:
- **~3.6GB is data the TUI genuinely retains for the life of the process** (GC can't touch it at any heap-pressure setting) — likely something eagerly initialized/decompressed at startup regardless of project content, since this reproduces identically against a completely empty project.
- **The other ~3GB on top of that (6.5GB total unconstrained) is ordinary reclaimable garbage** that just isn't being collected under default settings, presumably because Bun doesn't feel memory pressure when there's plenty of free RAM available, so the GC never runs proactively.

This might help split the fix into two parts: (1) find and reduce whatever's eagerly loaded into that ~3.6GB permanent floor — a heap snapshot from inside the process would likely nail the exact retainer, which I wasn't able to trigger non-interactively from a scripted session — and (2) separately, GC isn't being triggered proactively enough by default, which is masking the true "live" footprint and making the problem look worse than it structurally is.

In the meantime, `BUN_JSC_forceRAMSize` is a usable workaround for anyone hitting this hard — cuts real-world RAM pressure by close to half with no observed functional regression in my testing.

+1 — adding some prior art for this since it hasn't come up in the thread yet:

- **pi** ([earendil-works/pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi), formerly badlogic/pi-mono) does this out of the box: URLs in agent output are rendered as OSC 8 hyperlinks and cmd/ctrl+click follows them even while the TUI captures the mouse in fullscreen mode (their [terminal-setup docs](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/terminal-setup.md) call this out for Ghostty).
- The tmux ecosystem solves the same problem with selection-based fallbacks: [tmux-urlview](https://github.com/jaclu/tmux-urlview), [tmux-fzf-url](https://github.com/joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url), and [tmux-thumbs](https://github.com/tmux-plugins/tmux-thumbs).

Most modern terminals (iTerm2, Ghostty, Kitty, WezTerm) already handle cmd/ctrl+click on OSC 8 hyperlinks natively, so the main work is on the TUI side: emit OSC 8 sequences for URLs/paths and make sure mouse capture doesn't swallow the terminal's link-click gesture (see #44442) or degrade markdown links to `label (url)` (#45001).

For reference, there is an open implementation at #15631 (OSC 8 links for URLs and file paths in tool output) — CI is green but it has merge conflicts and is awaiting review.

CI is green across all checks, but this has merge conflicts and no reviews yet — is there anything blocking a maintainer look? #1168 is one of the longest-running feature requests and this PR is the main open implementation of it (its predecessor #7280 was marked `Fixes #1168`).

Happy to help with a rebase if that's what's holding it up.

For what it's worth, [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) ships this exact behavior in production (OSC 8 links in agent output that stay clickable even while the TUI captures the mouse), so there's good prior art that the approach works well in practice.

Follow-up with some concrete findings that affect this PR:

**It's based on `dev`, and the code has moved twice since March.**

1. On current `dev`, the paths this PR touches no longer exist — the TUI moved from `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/**` to `packages/opencode/src/cli/tui/**`, which is why GitHub reports merge conflicts.
2. More importantly, the upcoming `v2` line extracts the TUI into a dedicated `packages/tui` package with a different architecture (`src/routes/session`, `src/component`, `src/ui`, feature plugins), so a plain rebase onto `dev` would likely be throwaway work.

**Useful for anyone picking this up:** `v2` already ships the core primitive this PR builds on — `packages/tui/src/ui/link.tsx` renders OSC 8 hyperlinks (opentui `<a href>` plus an `onMouseUp` → `open()` fallback). It's currently only used in the auth/integration dialogs, not in assistant messages or tool output.

So the highest-value path here is probably retargeting/reworking this onto `v2`: reuse the existing `Link` primitive, and wire the URL/file-path detection (`TextWithLinks` equivalent) into message markdown rendering and tool output there. That would directly address #1168 where it matters going forward.

Happy to help with the retarget/rework if useful.

brew remove opencode
sudo cp dist/opencode-darwin-arm64/bin/opencode /usr/local/bin/

## Reproduction evidence: optional OAuth server appears connected but cannot authenticate in the TUI

### Environment

- OpenCode: `v2.0.3`
- OS: Windows 11 `10.0.26200.9445`
- Terminal: Windows Terminal, `TERM=xterm-256color`
- Shell: `C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe`
- Install: npm global, latest channel
- Active plugins: none found

### Reproduction

- Configure an OAuth-capable remote MCP server that also exposes public tools.
- Start OpenCode without stored OAuth credentials.
- `opencode mcp list` and `/mcps` report the server as `connected` because anonymous initialization and public tools succeed.
- Call an account-protected tool; it returns `Unauthorized`.
- Open `/mcps`. The server can only be connected or disconnected with Space. Enter exposes no detail view or Authenticate action.
- Run `opencode mcp auth <server>` externally and complete browser authorization.
- Call the same protected tool again; it succeeds.

### Expected behavior

The MCP modal should expose Authenticate/Re-authenticate for OAuth-capable remote servers even when their transport status is `connected`. Alternatively, a protected-tool authorization failure should transition the server to an actionable authentication-required state.

### Actual behavior

Anonymous connectivity masks the missing OAuth session. The TUI reports `connected` and offers no authentication path, leaving `opencode mcp auth <server>` as the only working route.

This reproduces consistently with Avails. It is also the same detection ambiguity noted in #26195: an MCP server can return HTTP 200 without authentication while protected operations still require OAuth.

### Why this matters
v2 prompt input silently ignores file drops after the first `@` mention — multi-file context never lands (#39705).

### Evidence
Tip `4ecb92b` (base `dev`):
- `packages/session-ui/src/v2/components/prompt-input/store.ts` — `addMention` used `lastIndexOf("@")` on joined text; now `mentionQueryStart()` (caret-anchored `/@(\S*)$/` in the cursor text part, else insert at cursor)
- `insertMention` clamps partial ranges

I can reproduce a closely related issue on Windows with OpenCode Desktop 1.18.31, and I have a full debug bundle containing multiple renderer-unresponsive samples.

### Environment

- OpenCode Desktop: 1.18.31
- OS: Windows x64
- Electron: 42.3.3
- Chrome: 148
- Node: 24.15

### What happens

When I paste a large technical prompt, report, or log directly into the OpenCode Desktop composer, the UI can become completely unresponsive.

This is a renderer/UI hang rather than a normal delay waiting for the model/provider.

My debug bundle contains multiple `renderer unresponsive` events. The captured stacks repeatedly point to the same prompt-editor path:

```text
HTMLDivElement.onPaste
→ PromptInputV2
→ parsePromptInputV2Editor
→ editor/node traversal
→ input/state updates
```

Other samples during the same type of freeze include:

```text
onPaste
→ input processing
→ setPrompt
→ JSON.stringify
→ reactive updates
```

The important point is that my Windows logs independently converge on the same `parsePromptInputV2Editor` / `onPaste` area reported in this issue.

### Observed timestamps

The debug logs contain several renderer-unresponsive events, including approximately:

```text
19:33:05  renderer unresponsive
19:47:13  renderer unresponsive
20:23:06  renderer unresponsive
00:39:06  renderer unresponsive
```

The last freeze occurred immediately before I exported the debug package.

### ResizeObserver activity

The renderer logs also contain a very large number of:

```text
ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.
```

messages during affected sessions.

I cannot prove that ResizeObserver activity is the root cause, but there appears to be significant layout/reactive churn around the same Desktop renderer sessions.

### Important distinction: hang vs crash

In my case I do not currently see evidence that the whole Desktop application process crashes.

The behavior is primarily:

```text
renderer hang / UI freeze
```

rather than:

```text
full process crash
```

The backend/agent can remain alive while the Desktop UI is unresponsive.

### Additional system-pressure finding

The same debug package also captured a separate Windows subprocess failure:

```text
0xC000012D
STATUS_COMMITMENT_LIMIT
```

followed shortly afterward by:

```text
0xC0000142
STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED
```

So the machine also experienced Windows virtual-memory pressure during a long-running development workload.

I consider that a secondary issue rather than the primary cause of the paste-specific renderer hangs, because the renderer stacks repeatedly identify the paste/editor path.

### Expected behavior

Large pasted input should not be able to synchronously block the Electron renderer.

Potential mitigations could include:

- moving expensive paste parsing/normalization off the renderer main thread where possible;
- chunking/yielding during large input processing;
- avoiding repeated whole-editor traversal or serialization;
- limiting unnecessary reactive/layout work;
- applying a safe large-paste threshold;
- warning the user when unusually large input is pasted;
- storing large pasted blocks in a more compact representation rather than continuously rendering/parsing the entire payload.

### Reproduction pattern

1. Open an existing OpenCode Desktop development session.
2. Copy a large technical prompt, log, audit report, or structured specification.
3. Paste it directly into the composer.
4. The UI becomes very slow or Windows reports the application as not responding.

I reproduced this, and I believe the diagnosis in the description points at the wrong variable. It isn't about the PDF containing an image — it's the **transport** opencode uses.

**Both PDFs you attached contain zero embedded images** (`pdfimages -list` returns 0 rows for each), and both still fail. Holding everything else constant and changing only the transport:

| Your attachment | `file_data` (what opencode sends) | `file_id` (upload first) |
|---|---|---|
| `PDF Failed to parse.pdf` (Quartz/macOS, 0 images) | 400 `1210` | **200** — *"Es un currículum vitae (CV) en francés…"* |
| `PDF Failed to parse - Libre office created.pdf` (LibreOffice 24.2, 0 images) | 400 `1210` | **200** — reads *"Test d'un pdf produit par…"* |

Same bytes, same API key, same model, same minute.

**Why.** Z.AI's OpenAPI for `POST /paas/v4/chat/completions` (`VisionMultimodalContentItem` → `File`) documents three members of `file`, and attaches the supported-format list — *"Supports formats such as pdf, txt, word, jsonl, xlsx, pptx"* — **only to `file_url`**. `file_id` is documented as GLM-5.3-Flash-only. `file_data` declares no format list at all.

`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` hardcodes `application/pdf` → `file_data`:

```js
if (part.mediaType === "application/pdf") {
  return { type: "file", file: {
    filename: part.filename ?? "document.pdf",
    file_data: `data:application/pdf;base64,${convert(part.data)}` }}
}
```

That is the one PDF route Z.AI rejects. Upload endpoint is `POST /paas/v4/files`, multipart, `purpose=user_data` — note `purpose=agent` also returns `1210`, so the purpose matters.

Full transport matrix, spec citations, controls ruling out `thinking` / `max_tokens` / account / network, and a minimal key-free repro are in #49237. Same root cause as #48868, which shows this is **not** zai-specific: the identical `file_data` mapping also breaks the `opencode-go` / zen gateway, there with a 422.

Two follow-ups on your report:

- **"one pdf is correctly accepted by GLM API via OpenCode"** — I could not get any PDF to succeed over `file_data`, including a 615-byte one I generated with no images. If you still have that file, it would be genuinely useful to know whether it went through `file_data` or took another path. That's the one observation my model doesn't explain.
- **Your "poisoned session" observation is correct and structural.** The attachment is stored in `state.attachments` on the tool part and replayed on every later turn, so a single rejected PDF keeps failing the session until it's removed from the DB. #48868 documents the same behaviour on a different provider.

Worth noting the diagnosis in the description was attributed to *"GLM analysis"* — asking the model to explain its own API error. That's how the image hypothesis got in; the attachments disprove it.

Cross-linking — the duplicate bot was right, and the scope is wider than I framed it.

- **#48868** (13 Sep) — same root cause, different blast radius: the identical `file_data` mapping breaks the `opencode-go` / zen gateway with a 422 (`messages.N.user.content.str`). So the condition is **not** "provider is `zai`" but "OpenAI-compatible provider that rejects PDFs over `file_data`". Worth folding into the fix design.
- **#49028** (14 Sep) — same symptom on `zai`, with two repro PDFs attached.

I ran those two attachments through the transport matrix ([comment](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/49028#issuecomment-5689126262)). Both contain **zero embedded images**, which disproves the "PDF contains an image" hypothesis in that thread, and both flip from 400 `1210` to a correct 200 when moved from `file_data` to `file_id` (`purpose=user_data`).

One open variable I cannot explain: #49028 reports that *one* PDF was accepted. I could not reproduce any `file_data` PDF succeeding, including a 615-byte image-free one. Flagging it so nobody treats my model as complete.

Happy for maintainers to consolidate these however is most useful — including closing this one in favour of #49028 or #48868. I kept the write-up here rather than duplicating it across three threads.

One further data point relevant to whether `file_id` is an acceptable fix, since PDF ingestion quality matters for anyone relying on it: on a two-column registry document (body text plus a left margin column of annotations), the `file_id` route returns the body in correct reading order with no margin contamination, and its output matches, word for word, an independent vision pass over the same page rendered to PNG. Naïve `pdftotext` on the same page interleaves the two columns. So Z.AI's server-side ingestion is not a naïve text extraction, and `file_id` preserves document fidelity.

**Update:** after deeper investigation this turned out to be a local configuration issue on my side, not an OpenCode/opentui bug. Closing it (sorry for the noise).

### Root cause

One of my TUI plugins (a voice plugin) registered its keybinds through a `normalizeBind()` helper that converted `<leader>r` into `leader+r`. V2's keymap parser reads `leader+r` as a **literal key sequence starting with `l`**, so `l` became a pending prefix and its first press was swallowed. That also explains the odd "one inserted per two presses" pattern. Fixing the plugin to register `<leader>r` (the same format V1 and the V2 docs use) resolves it completely.

### Evidence (OpenCode 2.0.3, Kitty 0.48.2, CachyOS)

- `OTUI_STDIN_LOG` shows Kitty sends `l` as the plain byte `0x6c` and that OpenCode **receives all 4** `l` presses — so nothing is lost in the terminal or the stdin parser.
- `a`/`b`/`n`/`p`/`c` insert 4/4; `l` inserts **2/4**.
- With no plugins at all: `l` inserts 4/4.
- With only that plugin loaded (original file): `l` inserts 2/4. With the binding corrected to `<leader>r`: 4/4.
- Minimal diagnostic: pressing `l` then `x` inserts only `x` when broken (the `l` is held as a prefix) vs `lx` when fixed.

So this is **not** the `cmd`/super-chord case from #47989 and not the CSI final-byte family: no `cmd`/super binding is required, and any plugin binding whose sequence starts with a literal `l` triggers it.

### Suggestion

A malformed binding such as `leader+r` (missing `<...>`) is currently accepted and silently expanded into literal key strokes. A validation warning for unknown tokens would have saved a lot of debugging time.
